canary.method: openpyxl writes formulas with NO cached <v> value, so the uploaded chunk workbooks contain zero cached results. Google Drive's auto-conversion to a Google Sheet recalculates every formula with Google's engine; exporting that Sheet back to .xlsx carries those computed values out. The deterministic canary =1111+2222 in Z1 of EVERY sheet reading back exactly 3333 therefore proves genuine computation -- without recalculation the cell would read back blank (None), since nothing was ever cached. The volatile =NOW() canary is recorded per chunk as corroboration, but UNLIKE the LibreOffice runner (which converts the same file twice and shows =NOW() differing) a single Drive import yields one timestamp, so no cross-run volatile comparison is possible: now_differs_across_runs is null by design, and the deterministic canary is the load-bearing proof here.

CEILING_libreoffice_default_mode_diverge.description: GOLD QUIRK CANDIDATE: identical 2-argument call (Mode omitted) with number and significance both negative. Per Microsoft's documented CEILING rule this must round AWAY from zero.
CEILING_libreoffice_default_mode_diverge.notes: Microsoft (https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/ceiling-function-0a5cd7c8-0720-4f0a-bd2c-c943e510899f): both-negative case rounds away from zero, so CEILING(-45.67,-2) -> -46 (ratio -45.67/-2=22.835, ceiling(22.835)=23, 23*-2=-46). LibreOffice's own CEILING docs (https://help.libreoffice.org/latest/en-US/text/scalc/01/func_ceiling.html) define a 3rd optional Mode argument that ONLY applies when both Number and Significance are negative, and state: 'if Mode is equal to zero or not given, negative numbers are rounded up (towards zero)' -- with LO's own worked example CEILING(-45.67;-2;0) = -44. That means the identical 2-arg formula (Mode omitted) is documented to resolve to -44 under LibreOffice's own default, vs -46 under Microsoft's documented default -- a genuine cross-engine default-behavior divergence for the exact same formula text, not just a wording difference. If LO's executed result is -44, matched_expected:false here is the intended, correct signal of that divergence -- do not 'fix' this expectation to match LO.

CEILING_nonnumeric_error.description: Nonnumeric first argument -> #VALUE!, per Microsoft docs: 'If either argument is nonnumeric, CEILING returns the #VALUE! error value.'

FLOOR_both_negative_toward_zero.notes: Microsoft's worked example table gives FLOOR(-2.5,-2) = -2 exactly (https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/floor-function-14bb497c-24f2-4e04-b327-b0b4de5a8886). Note this is the OPPOSITE rounding direction of CEILING(-2.5,-2)=-4 for the identical arguments -- FLOOR and CEILING deliberately diverge on both-negative inputs, not a bug.

FLOOR_mismatched_sign_error.description: Number positive, significance negative (opposite signs) -> #NUM!, explicitly documented by Microsoft: 'If Number is positive and Significance is negative, FLOOR returns the #NUM! error value.'

FLOOR_libreoffice_default_mode_divergenc.description: GOLD QUIRK CANDIDATE: mirror image of the CEILING default-Mode divergence. Both Number and significance negative, Mode omitted.
FLOOR_libreoffice_default_mode_divergenc.notes: Derived from Microsoft's own worked FLOOR(-2.5,-2)=-2 example (both-negative case rounds TOWARD zero): ratio -45.67/-2=22.835, truncating toward zero gives 22, 22*-2=-44. LibreOffice's own FLOOR docs (https://help.libreoffice.org/latest/en-US/text/scalc/01/func_floor.html) define an optional 3rd Mode argument that only applies when both Number and Significance are negative, stating 'Mode = 0 or omitted: negative numbers are rounded down (away from zero)' with LO's own worked example FLOOR(-45.67;-2;0) = -46. So the identical 2-arg formula (Mode omitted) is documented to resolve to -46 under LibreOffice's default vs -44 under Microsoft's documented behavior -- a genuine divergence, and the exact mirror image of the CEILING case above (there Excel defaults away-from-zero and LO defaults toward-zero; here Excel defaults toward-zero and LO defaults away-from-zero). If LO's executed result is -46, matched_expected:false is the correct, intended signal -- do not 'fix' this expectation to match LO.

FLOOR_nonnumeric_error.description: Nonnumeric first argument -> #VALUE!, per Microsoft docs: 'If either argument is nonnumeric, FLOOR returns the #VALUE! error value.'

FLOOR.MATH_basic_significance.description: Rounds 24.3 down to the nearest multiple of 5. Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/floor-math-function-c302b599-fbdb-4177-ba19-2c2b1249a2f5 (worked example table)

FLOOR.MATH_default_significance_1.description: Significance and mode both omitted -> defaults to nearest integer (significance 1). Source: Microsoft FLOOR.MATH docs.

FLOOR.MATH_negative_default_mode_away_fr.description: Negative number, mode omitted -> FLOOR.MATH's default for negative numbers rounds AWAY from zero (opposite default direction from CEILING.MATH's toward-zero default).
FLOOR.MATH_negative_default_mode_away_fr.notes: Microsoft worked example: FLOOR.MATH(-8.1,2) = -10 ('rounds -8.1 down (away from 0) to the nearest integer that is a multiple of 2'). Note this default is the mirror image of CEILING.MATH's default (toward zero) for the same-shaped call.

FLOOR.MATH_negative_mode_nonzero_toward_.notes: Microsoft worked example: FLOOR.MATH(-5.5,2,-1) = -4 ('rounds -5.5 toward 0 ... using a non-zero Mode, which reverses rounding direction').

MIN_basic.description: Smallest value in a simple numeric range

MIN_ignores_text.description: Text values in the range are ignored, not treated as 0

MINIFS_single_criteria.description: Min of A where paired B > 2

MINUTE_of_time_near_midnight.description: MINUTE just before a day boundary

MOD_negative_divisor.description: Negative divisor: result takes the sign of the divisor

MODE_basic_repeated_value.description: Basic case with one clearly most-frequent value
MODE_basic_repeated_value.notes: This is Microsoft's own documented MODE example data set -- https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/mode-function-e45192ce-9122-4980-82ed-4bdc34973120 -- 4 appears 3 times, more than any other value

MODE_no_repeated_value_na.description: When every value in the data set is unique (no duplicates at all), MODE has nothing to return

MODE_negative_numbers_repeated.description: MODE works the same way on negative numbers

MODE_ignores_text_and_blanks.description: Text values and blank cells in the range are ignored when finding the mode

MODE_MULT_two_modes.description: Returns every value tied for most frequent as a spilled vertical array; 1 and 2 each appear twice

MODE_MULT_single_mode.description: With one clear most-frequent value, returns just that value

MODE_SNGL_basic.description: Returns the single most frequently occurring value

MODE_SNGL_from_range.description: Most frequent value read from a cell range

MODE_SNGL_first_of_ties.description: When two values tie for most frequent, returns the one that appears first

MODE_SNGL_no_repeats_error.description: Errors when no value repeats. Excel and Google Sheets return #N/A here; LibreOffice Calc returns #VALUE! instead.

MONTH_of_date.description: MONTH applied to a constructed date

MONTH_ignores_time_fraction.description: A serial with a fractional (time-of-day) component still resolves to the correct calendar month

MROUND_both_negative.description: Both arguments negative (same sign, as required) -> rounds to nearest multiple, sign preserved. Source: Microsoft MROUND docs worked example.

MROUND_fractional_multiple.description: Rounds 1.3 to the nearest multiple of the fractional value 0.2. Source: Microsoft MROUND docs worked example.

MROUND_mismatched_signs_error.description: Number and multiple must have the same sign, per Microsoft docs: 'The Number and Multiple arguments must have the same sign. If not, a #NUM error is returned.'

MROUND_zero.description: Zero rounds to zero regardless of the multiple.

MULTINOMIAL_two_groups.description: Ratio of the factorial of the sum to the product of factorials: 5!/(2!3!) = 10

N_true.description: TRUE -> 1, per Microsoft's N doc example table

N_false.description: FALSE -> 0, per the same doc's TRUE/FALSE convention

NETWORKDAYS_INTL_july.description: Working days in July 2026 with default weekend

NOMINAL_inverse_of_effect.description: Inverting EFFECT recovers the 6% nominal rate

NOT_zero_coercion.description: 0 coerces to FALSE, so NOT(0) -> TRUE (same numeric-coercion convention as AND/OR/XOR)
NOT_zero_coercion.notes: Numeric coercion for logical functions confirmed via https://www.ablebits.com/office-addins-blog/excel-and-or-xor-not-functions/

NOT_nonzero_coercion.description: Any nonzero number coerces to TRUE, so NOT(5) -> FALSE

NOT_text_error.description: An arbitrary text literal cannot be coerced to a logical value -> #VALUE!

NOW_exists_and_plausible.description: Existence probe only: NOW() is volatile (changes every recalculation), so there is no fixed expected value
NOW_exists_and_plausible.notes: Non-deterministic by design; only check the engine recognizes the function and returns a plausible date-time serial

NOW_self_difference_is_deterministic.description: Two NOW() calls inside one cell evaluate in the same recalculation pass, so their difference is exactly 0 — a deterministic assertion about a volatile function (N() keeps the result a plain number instead of a duration-formatted cell)

NOW_on_or_after_today.description: NOW() includes today's date plus a time fraction, so it is always >= TODAY() within one recalculation

NPER_payoff_periods.description: Years to pay off 5000 at 10% with 1000/period: -ln(1-r*PV/pmt)/ln(1+r) = 7.2725

NPV_three_cashflows.description: 100/1.1 + 200/1.1^2 + 300/1.1^3 = 481.59 (NPV discounts the FIRST argument one period)

NUMBERVALUE_basic.description: Basic numeric text conversion with explicit US-style decimal_separator and group_separator arguments

NUMBERVALUE_european_separators.notes: Matches Microsoft's own documented example. Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/numbervalue-function-1b05c8cf-2bfa-4437-af70-596c7ea7d879; MISMATCH vs expected: expected 2500.27, got '#NAME?'

NUMBERVALUE_malformed_text.description: Text that cannot be parsed as a number at all -> #VALUE!
NUMBERVALUE_malformed_text.notes: Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/numbervalue-function-1b05c8cf-2bfa-4437-af70-596c7ea7d879 - 'If any of the arguments are not valid, NUMBERVALUE returns the #VALUE! error value'; MISMATCH vs expected: expected '#VALUE!', got '#NAME?'

NUMBERVALUE_decimal_separator_used_twice.description: A decimal separator appearing more than once in the text is documented as invalid input -> #VALUE!
NUMBERVALUE_decimal_separator_used_twice.notes: Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/numbervalue-function-1b05c8cf-2bfa-4437-af70-596c7ea7d879 - decimal separator used multiple times is explicitly called out as an error condition; MISMATCH vs expected: expected '#VALUE!', got '#NAME?'

OCT2BIN_padded.description: The optional places argument pads the binary result to a fixed width

OCT2DEC_roundtrip.description: OCT2DEC reverses DEC2OCT, recovering the original number

ODD_round_up.description: Rounds up to the nearest odd integer

OFFSET_zero_offset_returns_same_cell.description: rows=0, cols=0 returns a reference to the exact starting cell

OR_range_numeric_with_nonzero.description: A range of numbers is coerced to logical (0=FALSE, nonzero=TRUE); one nonzero value makes the whole OR TRUE

OR_range_numeric_all_zero.description: A range of all-zero numbers coerces to all-FALSE -> FALSE

OR_range_text_ignored.description: Text within a range argument is ignored (not coerced, not an error), per https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/or-function-7d17ad14-8700-4281-b308-00b131e22af0: 'If an array or reference argument contains text or empty cells, those values are ignored.'

PEARSON_perfect_positive.description: Perfectly linear, same-direction data gives a correlation of 1

PEARSON_perfect_negative.description: Perfectly linear, opposite-direction data gives a correlation of -1

PEARSON_no_correlation.description: A symmetric pattern with no linear trend gives a correlation of 0. PEARSON returns the identical coefficient as CORREL.

PERCENTILE.INC_k_half.description: k=0.5 (median); compare to PERCENTILE.EXC_k_half on identical data

PMT_standard_mortgage.description: Monthly payment on a $300k 30-year loan at 6% annual: the standard amortization formula gives $1,798.65

POWER_negative_exponent.description: Negative exponent gives a reciprocal power

POWER_fractional_exponent_positive_base.description: Fractional exponent on a positive base is a well-defined real root (square root here)

POWER_negative_base_fractional_exponent.description: A negative base raised to a non-integer exponent has no real-number result in general (would require complex numbers), so Excel errors
POWER_negative_base_fractional_exponent.notes: Confirmed via Microsoft's own community support: entering =(-8)^(2/3) (equivalent power semantics to POWER) returns #NUM! in Excel -- https://answers.microsoft.com/en-us/msoffice/forum/all/excel-calculating-exponential-of-negative-number/5c67eae2-5682-4daf-b3d6-50b22e9919c2 -- note that -8^(1/3) is mathematically -2 as a real cube root, but Excel's POWER/^ implementation does not special-case rational exponents with odd integer denominators and returns #NUM! for any negative base with a non-integer exponent; MISMATCH vs expected: expected '#NUM!', got -2

POWER_zero_to_zero.description: 0 raised to the 0th power; by the near-universal 'empty product' convention this is 1 (matches VBA's own '0^0', Python, C#, and LibreOffice/OpenOffice Calc)
POWER_zero_to_zero.notes: Real Excel (the worksheet function, and even the '^' operator) has a long-standing, Microsoft-acknowledged bug -- reproduced in Excel 2007 and 2010 and still reported unresolved -- where both '=0^0' and '=POWER(0,0)' incorrectly return #NUM! instead of 1, even though VBA's own 'x = 0 ^ 0' correctly evaluates to 1 in the same product. Recording the spec/cross-engine-consensus value (1) as 'expected' here so this exact Excel quirk shows up as a flagged divergence rather than being silently baked in as 'correct' -- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/4850441/excel-formula-bug-00-gives-num

PPMT_first_month_principal.description: First-month principal: total payment 1798.65 minus 1500 interest

PROPER_apostrophe_word_boundary.description: PROPER treats an apostrophe as a word boundary too, capitalizing the letter that follows it -- so a name like o'brien becomes O'Brien. RANDBETWEEN_degenerate_equal_bounds.description: When bottom==top the result is deterministic

RANDBETWEEN_negative_range.description: Existence probe with an all-negative range

RANK.EQ_tie_shares_top_rank.description: Like legacy RANK, ties get the same top rank (contrast with RANK.AVG's averaged rank on identical data, see RANK.AVG_tie_averages_ranks)
